data.name: Devji
data.gender_notes: Devji is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Devji is a Hindu name derived from the Sanskrit language. It is a compound name, consisting of the prefix 'Deva' meaning 'god' and the suffix 'ji' which is a term of respect. The name signifies the one who is the god of all gods, often referred to as Lord Shiva or Mahadev. The name Devji carries the meaning “God of Gods” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Devji usually hope their child will grow to embody god of gods and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of divine power and protection
data.etymology: Devji belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Gods.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Devji total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: Devji is a revered name in Hindu culture, representing the divine presence and power of Lord Shiva, who is considered the god of gods. In various traditional stories and folklore, Devji is employed as a protector and a giver of blessings. Many Hindu families may name their child Devji as a symbol of devotion and respect towards Lord Shiva.
data.spiritual_significance: Devji holds immense spiritual significance in Hinduism. It symbolizes one's deep connection with the divine and the ultimate reality, expressed as Lord Shiva. It signifies the belief that God is the supreme power, the unchanging and eternal being, who protects, sustains and guides us in our lives. Devji embodies the qualities of peace, tranquility, and pure love - qualities that an individual may aspire to embody in their own lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Devji: God of Gods. The name Devji embodies the divine presence and absolute power of Lord God. It is a symbol of devotion, faith, and surrender to the Almighty.

historical_references.reference: Devji was a popular deity in the medieval Chalukya and Hoysala periods of Karnataka, India. He was a form of Vishnu and was especially revered in the regions of Mysore and Coorg.
historical_references.context: Medieval Chalukya and Hoysala empires of Karnataka, India

historical_references.reference: Devji was also known as 'Deva Kadamba' and was the presiding deity of the Kadamba dynasty. He was believed to have been the protector of the dynasty and its kings.
historical_references.context: Early Kadamba dynasty of South India
